temperature-converter.quickAnswer: Type a temperature in any of the three scales and the other two update immediately. Temperature uses offset formulas rather than simple ratios, so each field stays in sync with exact conversions like °F = °C × 9/5 + 32.
keyFacts: Celsius sets 0° at water freezing and 100° at water boiling (at sea level).
Fahrenheit sets 32° at water freezing and 212° at boiling; it is still standard in the US.
Kelvin starts at absolute zero (−273.15 °C) and is the SI unit for thermodynamics.
−40° is the point where Celsius and Fahrenheit read the same number.
A change of 1 kelvin equals a change of 1 degree Celsius; a change of 1 °F is 5/9 of that.
howTo: Type a temperature into any one of the three fields.
The other two fields update automatically and instantly.
Values below absolute zero are not allowed and get clamped.
Use the reference table to sanity-check common points.
Copy any field value for use in recipes, weather or lab work.
temperature-converter.workedExample:
Convert 25 °C to Fahrenheit and Kelvin.
Step 1: °F = 25 × 9/5 + 32 = 45 + 32 = 77 °F.
Step 2: K = 25 + 273.15 = 298.15 K.
Answer: 25 °C = 77 °F = 298.15 K.
benefits: All three scales live-synced — edit any field.
Reference table covers absolute zero, freezing, body and boiling points.
Exact formulas, no rounding until display.

limitations: Display is rounded to 2 decimal places.

Rankine and Réaumur scales are not included in this version.
Everyday weather accuracy does not need more than 1 decimal place.

faqs.q: How do I convert Celsius to Fahrenheit?
At what temperature are Celsius and Fahrenheit equal?
faqs.a: At −40°. −40 °C = −40 °F. It is the only point where the two scales agree.
0 K = −273.15 °C = −459.67 °F. It is the lowest temperature physically possible; nothing can be colder.
Kelvin is used in science and engineering because it starts at absolute zero, which makes gas laws and thermodynamic formulas work without offsets.
